current.text: Randle plays for Brooklyn now. He came over in the Nic Claxton trade.
He is projected to start at forward next to Mikel Brown Jr., Egor Demin, Michael Porter Jr. and Day'Ron Sharpe.
He is the Nets' most accomplished on-ball creator and is expected to handle the ball a lot.
He has several years left on his contract and is expected to stay in Brooklyn.

Experts expect his usage to rise from about 27 to about 30, with more assists, because he shares the ball with Michael Porter Jr. instead of playing behind Anthony Edwards. His defensive stats are not expected to improve.
Experts expect his minutes to drop to about 32 from 34 to 35 last season. Blowouts and minutes for young frontcourt players such as Noah Clowney lower his upside.
Brooklyn does not own its draft pick (Houston does), so it has no reason to tank. It also has little reason to win beyond player development.
Brooklyn may rest him for some games late in the season, mainly in March, to give the young players time. That overlaps our fantasy playoffs.

Experts disagree on his category rank. One projects him 55 to 75, probably 65 to 70, and says to take him a bit later in category leagues than in points leagues. A newer note says he can be top 50 again and is good value at a rank of 73.
His ESPN rank of 86 is called great value, and his Yahoo ADP around 68 is called fair value.
In an expert auction mock, he went for 15 USD. The expert had hoped to pay about 10 USD.
His block rate of 4.9% last season was well below his 9% career rate. It might recover in Brooklyn now that he does not play next to Gobert.
Brooklyn has 16 back-to-backs, tied with Boston for the most in the league. For a season ending March 28, its playoff schedule is 3-4-3 games, with only one back-to-back in the playoff weeks.
Brooklyn is projected to win about 28 games, with a range of about 22 to 30.

durable.text: He is worth more in points leagues than in 9-cat leagues. One expert still says category leagues underrate him.
He turns the ball over a lot. TO is his clearly weakest category, far worse than the league and his position.
He gives few defensive stats. His steals are about average and his blocks are poor.
Points, rebounds and assists are his strengths, and his assists are high for a forward.
On average his FG% and FT% are neutral, not harmful, despite his reputation. But they swing a lot from season to season.
He shot 32% from three in Minnesota, and defenses treated him as a non-shooter.

note: Randle is a points, rebounds and assists forward who costs you in turnovers (TO z -1.8). That makes him a natural fit for punt TO builds. He does not hurt you in FG% or FT% on average, but they swing a lot. His market sits around rank 73 to 86, and average costs are about 8 USD on both sites. Our league paid 10 USD last season and an expert mock went to 15 USD, so 10 to 14 USD is a fair range. Early in the season, check whether he really gets about 30% usage in about 32 minutes. Brooklyn may rest him in March, which would cut into our weeks 19 to 21, so consider trading him before the 2027-03-04 deadline.
